title: The Atlas Computer and the Invention of Virtual Memory (1959-1962)
explainer: Before virtual memory existed, programmers on early Manchester machines wrote their own manual 'overlay' code to shuttle data between a small fast store and a slower one whenever a program outgrew physical RAM. Tom Kilburn's team on the Atlas computer automated that swapping in hardware and supervisor software, calling it 'one-level storage' in their 1962 paper - the scheme that modern paging and virtual memory, central to this lesson, directly descend from.
